newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World Bank urges Bangladesh to usher in reforms.
newsitem.headline: World Bank urges Bangladesh to usher in reforms.

text.p: Bangladesh faces a long and difficult task in implementing economic reforms despite political commitments by the country's government, the World Bank said in a report seen in Dhaka on Saturday.
The bank, which will sponsor a donors meeting in Dhaka later this month, said the democratically-elected government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina should rapidly complete privatisation programmes.
Hasina should also push harder to usher in her reform plans, World Bank president James Wolfensohn said in the report to Hasina's government, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.

"We have urged rapid completion of privatisation programmes and delegation of greater responsibility for personnel and financial decisions to operational managers as the milestones for the near term," Wolfensohn said.

"Overcoming institutional weaknesses that dampen the pace of reforms will continue to be a complex, time-consuming, and high priority task that is not amenable to quick fixes, requiring us and a committed government to stay on the course," he said.
"The next 12 months should tell how well the new government has used the opportunities for making a difference."
Wolfensohn's report described public sector reforms in Bangladesh as "politically sensitive, institutionally complex, and likely to remain a major challenge."
The bank will sponsor a two-day aid donors meeting in Dhaka starting on February 25.

The report said the World Bank's "assistance strategy addresses the risks faced by the Awami League government through close monitoring and collaboration with the International Monetary Fund on macroeconomic developments.
"Poverty on the scale seen in Bangladesh is not just a poverty of the people, but much more...of institutions unable to carry out programmes effectively," the bank said.
"We will intensify our efforts using events such as the upcoming ... review of the programmes."
World Bank officials in Dhaka said a proposed visit to Bangladesh by Wolfensohn in March had been postponed.
"Now the visit might be held in the early part of the autumn," one bank official told Reuters on Saturday.
He said Wolfensohn would meet Prime Minister Hasina and the ministers of finance, energy and industry.
He will also visit some World Bank-aided projects outside Dhaka.
